newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares lose legs late to close with softer bias.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares lose legs late to close with softer bias.

text.p: * NZ shares end narrowly softer after fairly busy day
* Some late profit-taking turns tone at the end
* Carter Holt Harvey continues tumble after recent gains
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -3.47 at 2,367.55
136 nil * NZSE-10 cap index -2.16 at 1,194.22
346 -7 * NZSC cap index -0.02 at 5,115.08

717 +1 * Other movers - -2

New Zealand share prices turned down towards the end of a lively session on Tuesday to leave key indices just below their previous closing levels and paint an unjustly soft picture of the market, dealers said.
"It doesn't necessarily look that bad, really the market did quite well but slipped back just at the close. There was some profit taking but nothing too dramatic," one share broker said.

The NZSE40 index closed 3.47 points, or 0.15 percent, off at 2,367.55. Dealers said there was evidence of some portfolio buying during the day and brewer Lion Nathan had risen on steady overseas demand to close up five cents at NZ$3.72.
Market leader Telecom added one cent on the day to finish at $7.17 in solid turnover.
Carter Holt Harvey eased in what brokers said was a correction to a sharp run-up over the last two months.
The forest products group ended off seven cents at $3.46, following on from a three-cent fall on Monday.
But brokers said the stock had enjoyed a very strong run, particularly last week when it hit a high of NZ$3.60 -- a level not seen since October 1995.
"This brought some selling out, clearly, and they've come back a bit," said John Rattray at Ord Minnett Securities.
"You might rather ask what it was to put them up so much, but I guess that's a sentiment change towards pulp and paper," he said.
CHH started April at NZ$3.00, then began appreciating on the view the international pulp and paper sector may have turned the corner.
Fletcher Paper had experienced a similar but smaller trend, peaking last week at NZ$3.42 and closing today at $3.36, down one cent on Monday's close.
